source_cards.back: Adding the motorcycle (M) endorsement to an existing license takes the motorcycle written test, vision and road sign tests, and a skills test on a motorcycle or motortricycle.

source_cards.front: How early may you renew, and which tests come with every renewal?

source_cards.front: What happens if you renew more than six months after expiration?

source_cards.front: When can a non-commercial driver renew while suspended or revoked?

needs.title: Intersections and right-of-way

source_cards.front: Does right-of-way law ever give a driver the right-of-way?
source_cards.back: Right-of-way law only says who must yield and never gives any driver the right-of-way, so you must do everything possible to avoid striking a pedestrian or vehicle no matter the circumstances.

source_cards.front: Where do right-of-way rules apply, and what do they decide?
source_cards.back: Right-of-way rules exist for places where vehicles or pedestrians are likely to meet and no signs or signals control traffic, and they say who goes first and who waits.

source_cards.front: At a four-way stop, who goes first?
source_cards.back: At a four-way stop, the driver who reaches the intersection first goes first, after stopping completely.

source_cards.front: Who goes first at a four-way stop, an uncontrolled intersection and a roundabout?
source_cards.back: A four-way stop goes by arrival order, an uncontrolled intersection goes to the vehicle on the right, and a roundabout goes to traffic already in the circle.

source_cards.front: How should you drive once you are inside a roundabout?
source_cards.back: While driving through a roundabout, keep right of the center island, yield the right-of-way to circulating vehicles, never change lanes or try to pass any vehicle, and do not stop unless stopping is the only way to avoid a crash.

source_cards.front: Near which crossings, and with which line, may you not drive left of center?
source_cards.back: Do not drive left of center within one hundred feet of or at an intersection or railroad grade crossing, or anywhere a solid yellow line is present.

source_cards.front: With no signs or lane markings, which lane do you turn from and into?
source_cards.back: With no signs or lane markings, turn from the lane nearest the direction you are heading into the lane nearest the one you left, then change lanes afterward if needed.

source_cards.front: Turning from a two-way street onto another two-way street, where do you keep your wheels and enter?
source_cards.back: Turning from a two-way street onto another two-way street, keep your left wheels as close as possible to the yellow line and enter to the right of the center line, using the right lane of a four-lane road if it is free.

source_cards.front: With two left-turn lanes, which lane does each car enter?
source_cards.back: With two left-turn lanes, a car in the left-side turn lane enters the left lane just right of the yellow line, and a car in the right-side turn lane enters the right lane.

needs.title: Roundabout approach and movement

source_cards.front: At an intersection with no stop sign or signal, other than a roundabout, whom do you yield to?
source_cards.back: At an intersection with no stop sign or signal, other than a roundabout, yield to vehicles coming from your right.

source_cards.front: Approaching a roundabout, whom do you yield to before entering?
source_cards.back: Approaching a roundabout, yield to traffic already circulating and to pedestrians in the crosswalks, and wait for a gap before entering.

source_cards.front: Who goes first at a four-way stop, an uncontrolled intersection and a roundabout?
source_cards.back: A four-way stop goes by arrival order, an uncontrolled intersection goes to the vehicle on the right, and a roundabout goes to traffic already in the circle.

source_cards.front: Which way do you travel around a roundabout, and whom do you yield to?
source_cards.back: At a roundabout you make a slight right turn and travel counterclockwise around the center island, yielding to traffic in the circle, bicyclists and pedestrians in the crosswalks.

source_cards.front: How should you approach a roundabout?
source_cards.back: Slow down before a roundabout, follow signs and markings to the correct lane in a multi-lane one, look left as you approach, and never make a left turn to enter.

source_cards.front: How should you drive once you are inside a roundabout?
source_cards.back: While driving through a roundabout, keep right of the center island, yield the right-of-way to circulating vehicles, never change lanes or try to pass any vehicle, and do not stop unless stopping is the only way to avoid a crash.

source_cards.front: How should you leave a roundabout?
source_cards.back: Leave a roundabout at a slow speed with your right turn signal on, and do not speed up until you are past the exit's pedestrian crossing.

source_cards.front: What do you do about an emergency vehicle near a roundabout?
source_cards.back: Do not enter a roundabout when an emergency vehicle is approaching, and if one comes while you are inside, exit immediately and pull to the right.

source_cards.front: What do you do if you miss your roundabout exit, and how do you treat trucks?
source_cards.back: If you miss your exit in a roundabout, keep circling until you reach it, and give trucks and trailers room because they may use more than one lane.

source_cards.front: What is a truck apron, and who may use it?
source_cards.back: A truck apron is the paved inner area of a roundabout for the rear wheels of large trucks, and cars, SUVs and pickup trucks must not use it.

source_cards.front: How many points does a conviction for failing to stop for a school bus carry?

source_cards.front: What suspensions apply for failing to stop for a school bus?

source_cards.front: How do you turn right when a cyclist is ahead of you?

source_cards.front: When turning left, when must you yield to an oncoming cyclist?

source_cards.front: How much room do you give a bicycle or moped when passing?

source_cards.front: What is a bicycle lane, and when may you cross it?

source_cards.front: What should you check before opening a car door into a traffic or bike lane?

source_cards.back: With three or more lanes going your way, stay in the right lane except to pass, but use the center lane if a lot of traffic is entering the right lane.

source_cards.front: If a traffic officer signals you to stop at a green light, what do you do?
source_cards.back: Always obey a traffic officer over any sign or signal, so if an officer signals you to stop at a green light, you stop.

source_cards.front: What does a flashing red light mean, and what does a flashing yellow light mean?
source_cards.back: A flashing red light has the same meaning as a stop sign, and a flashing yellow light means slow down and go ahead with caution.

source_cards.front: At a steady red light, where do you stop and how long do you wait?
source_cards.back: At a steady red light, stop at the stop line, the crosswalk or before the intersection and wait for green unless you are turning right.

source_cards.front: What does a steady yellow light warn, and when should you still go through?
source_cards.back: A steady yellow light warns that the signal is about to turn red, so stop unless you are already in the intersection or too close to stop safely.

source_cards.front: What does a green light let you do, and whom must you yield to first?
source_cards.back: A green light lets you go through, but first yield to vehicles and pedestrians still in the intersection.

source_cards.front: How does a flashing red signal differ from a steady red?
source_cards.back: A flashing red signal works like a stop sign, while a steady red means stop and wait for green except for a permitted right turn.

source_cards.front: How does a flashing yellow light differ from a steady yellow?
source_cards.back: A flashing yellow light means slow and proceed with caution, while a steady yellow means the light is about to turn red and you should stop if you safely can.

source_cards.front: How do you treat a traffic signal that is dark or not working?
source_cards.back: A traffic signal that is dark or not working is treated as a four-way stop.

source_cards.front: What do you get in a permissive left-turn phase, and what must you wait for?
source_cards.back: In a permissive left-turn phase you get a circular green or a flashing yellow arrow and must wait for a big enough gap in oncoming traffic.

source_cards.front: When do you turn in a protected left-turn phase, and what holds oncoming traffic?
source_cards.back: In a protected left-turn phase you turn only on a green arrow while oncoming traffic is held by a red light.

source_cards.front: What does a protected and permissive phase alternate between, and when must you pick a gap yourself?
source_cards.back: A protected and permissive phase alternates between a green arrow and a circular green or flashing yellow arrow, when you must pick a gap yourself.

source_cards.front: What does a steady red arrow mean, and whom may you still need to yield to?
source_cards.back: A steady red arrow means stop and wait for green or a flashing yellow arrow, and you may still need to yield to pedestrians.

source_cards.front: What does a steady yellow arrow follow, what can it change to, and how should you respond?
source_cards.back: A steady yellow arrow follows a green arrow and warns it will change to a circular green, a flashing yellow arrow or red, so be ready to yield or stop.

source_cards.front: What does a flashing yellow arrow let you do, and on what conditions?
source_cards.back: A flashing yellow arrow lets you turn in the arrow's direction, but only after a safe gap in oncoming traffic opens and while yielding to pedestrians.

source_cards.front: What does a green arrow let you do, and what conditions must hold?
source_cards.back: A green arrow lets you go the way it points, provided you are in the proper lane and no traffic or pedestrians are in your path.

source_cards.front: How does a green arrow differ from a flashing yellow arrow?
source_cards.back: A green arrow gives a clear path in its direction, while a flashing yellow arrow allows the turn only after you find a gap and yield.

source_cards.front: How does a steady red arrow differ from a steady yellow arrow?
source_cards.back: A steady red arrow means wait, but a steady yellow arrow means the green arrow is ending and you should get ready to yield or stop.

source_cards.front: What do the Stop Ahead and Signal Ahead signs warn of, and how should you prepare?
source_cards.back: A Stop Ahead sign means a stop sign is coming on your road, and a Signal Ahead sign means a traffic light is coming; be ready to stop for either.

needs.title: Skid and traction recovery

source_cards.front: How should you brake on slippery roads, and what does the guide say about very slick surfaces?
source_cards.back: Brake gently and smoothly on slippery roads; slamming the brakes can cause a skid, and on very slick surfaces you pump the brakes unless your manual gives anti-lock instructions.

source_cards.front: What is hydroplaning, and at what speeds can it happen?
source_cards.back: Hydroplaning is when tires ride on water instead of the road; it can happen at any speed over thirty-five miles per hour, and in a heavy storm tires can lose all contact at fifty-five miles per hour

source_cards.front: Which speed marks the start of hydroplaning, and which marks full loss of contact in a severe storm?
source_cards.back: Hydroplaning can begin above thirty-five miles per hour, while full loss of road contact in a severe storm can come at fifty-five miles per hour

source_cards.front: What should you do if you think you are hydroplaning?
source_cards.back: If you think you are hydroplaning, ease off the accelerator and slow down without braking, which could cause a skid.

source_cards.front: How do you prevent hydroplaning?
source_cards.back: Prevent hydroplaning with good, deep-tread tires at proper pressure, slower speeds in rain, and no cruise control.

source_cards.front: Does handling a skid differ between front-wheel and rear-wheel drive, and what are the first steps?
source_cards.back: A skid is handled the same way in front-wheel and rear-wheel drive vehicles: lift off the accelerator and do not hit the brakes.

source_cards.front: Which way do you steer in a skid, and what should you avoid?
source_cards.back: In a skid, gently steer in the direction the rear wheels are sliding, without braking hard or jerking the wheel, which only makes it worse.

source_cards.front: What four steps does the guide's skid diagram caption?
source_cards.back: The guide's skid diagram is captioned in four steps: before the skid, rear wheels sliding right, front wheels turned right, and the vehicle straight again.
